title: Discrete recurrence of the Hausdorff dimension
html:
d_{H,q}^{(n+1)} = d_{H,q}^{(n)} + \frac{(2q_n - 1)(3 - 4q_n)(q_n - 1)}{q_n^5}.

This defines a contraction mapping for q > 3/4. The iteration d_{H,q} \to d_{H,q} + \Delta d_{H,q} flows monotonically toward d_{H,q} = 0. The fractal complexity of the Reeb dynamics decreases with increasing q, vanishing at q \to \infty (the Big Bang, where the Julia set collapses to a point). The direction of decreasing d_{H,q} coincides with increasing q — pointing from the classical regime (q \to 1, maximal d_{H,q}) toward the Big Bang.

Regime table. See Table 1.

The q-deformed d_{H,q} and the classical Hausdorff dimension d_H of the Julia set over \mathbb{C} are distinct quantities (classical Hausdorff dimension comparison).

Convergence from local q. The downward iteration q_{n+1} = q_n - \hbar_{q_n} = (q_n^2 - q_n + 1)/q_n flows q toward the classical limit q = 1. This is a superattracting fixed point. Starting from our local q_0:

See Table 3.

It takes three Planck steps from our universe to reach the classical limit. The convergence is superlinear. At the fixed point, \eta_q = 1 nat, meaning each Reeb operation carries exactly one natural unit of information.

Cosmological arrow of time. The monotone decrease of d_{H,q} with q defines an information-theoretic arrow. Forward in time the parameter q flows from the Big Bang (q large) toward the classical limit q = 1 — the downward iteration above — so d_{H,q} increases along it. Reversing time reverses the discrete recurrence. The second law of thermodynamics asserts that the q-deformed dimension increases as q decreases.
